claims.text: MoS2 or a similar transition-metal dichalcogenide can serve as the lubricious phase in the proposed refractory-matrix composite.
A refractory-matrix composite containing uniformly dispersed nano- or micro-lamellar lubricious material will exhibit a stable low friction coefficient over a wide temperature range.
The proposed hierarchical composite will maintain high mechanical strength over a wide temperature range.
Conventionally processed refractory ceramics or intermetallics without an integrated lubricious phase typically suffer from high friction or compromised strength under extreme conditions.
A uniform hierarchical distribution of lamellae within a load-bearing matrix disperses stress.
A uniform hierarchical distribution of lubricious lamellae provides continuous surface lubrication.
The high-strength refractory matrix acts as the load-bearing component during sliding.
Dispersed lubricious lamellae form microscale lubrication layers under sliding contact.
The combined load-bearing and lubrication roles reduce friction.
The combined load-bearing and lubrication roles reduce wear.
Hierarchical interfaces can relieve stress concentrations and help preserve mechanical integrity.
The proposed composite will have a significantly lower sliding friction coefficient than the unmodified refractory matrix.
The proposed composite will have better wear resistance than the unmodified refractory matrix.
The proposed composite will avoid substantial mechanical-strength loss from room temperature to approximately 800 degrees Celsius or higher.
Nonuniform dispersion of the lubricious phase can prevent the intended balance of lubrication and mechanical strength.
Loss of lubricious-phase stability at high temperature can prevent the intended balance of lubrication and mechanical strength.
Excessive lubricious-phase content can undermine matrix integrity.
